Sofia — here are the bullets I recommend we include in the playbook and two sketch options summarized: 

Playbook bullets (short):
- Authentication: Customer-managed IdP to the control plane + mTLS between runtime nodes.
- Networking: Isolate inference clusters in private subnets; route egress via NAT Gateway or explicit proxy per policy. Recommend PrivateLink for cross-account model retrieval to avoid internet egress.
- Audit & Logging: Forward inference access logs to customer-managed SIEM (we support S3/HTTPS sinks). Enable token-level tracing only when required.
- Minimum hardening: Restrict management planes to jump hosts / bastion via MFA + IP allowlist; no public ingress to inference endpoints.

Sketch A — VPC-first (recommended for fastest time-to-value):
- Two VPCs (customer / redwood) with PrivateLink endpoints.
- Private subnets host inference; control plane in customer-managed VPC with peering or PrivateLink for API calls.
- Benefits: lower ops burden, supports KMS via IAM roles and customer-managed keys.

Sketch B — Airgapped on-prem variant:
- On-prem clusters in isolated network with one-way data egress via signed S3 objects or secure physical transfer for model weights.
- Redwood runtime runs in airgapped mode with local KV cache; control-plane optionally via temporary outbound bridge for updates.
- Benefits: maximal isolation, higher ops cost, longer lead time.

KMS / HSM notes (Jordan to confirm exact steps):
- We support CMK (customer-managed) with AWS KMS and can integrate with external HSM via KMIP if required. Expect additional setup for key ceremony and periodic audits.

I will put these into a 2-page PDF and add a simple PNG sketch (redwood_vpc_sketch_v1.png). Jordan — please add the HSM technical bullets when you have a minute.
